files.html: // examples/hello_world.zig - a first look at zimr. // Renders "Hello, World!" with the default font, a circle that // follows the mouse (or a finger), and a UI window whose slider // sets the circle's radius: text, shapes, input and immediate-mode // UI, each in a few lines. const std = @import("std"); const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator; const z = @import("zimr"); const zm = @import("zm"); const Color = zm.Color; const Vec2 = zm.Vec2; const float = zm.float; const State = struct { font: z.Font, /// The immediate-mode UI (`z.ui_real`): it keeps what the UI remembers between frames - where its windows are, /// which widget is being dragged. ui_host: z.UiHost, /// The circle's radius in CSS pixels, set by the UI's slider. circle_radius: f32 = 30, }; /// User-owned framework integration point. See `examples/basic.zig` /// for the canonical comment block; this declaration is the /// AppBridge pattern's required convention. const atkinson_mono_ttf = @embedFile("atkinson_mono_ttf"); fn deinit(gpa: Allocator, s: *State) void { s.ui_host.deinit(); z.unloadFont(gpa, s.font); } fn initState(gpa: Allocator, f: *z.Frame, s: *State) !void { const font: z.Font = try z.loadFont(f, gpa, atkinson_mono_ttf, 32); s.* = .{ .font = font, .ui_host = z.UiHost.init(gpa, font), }; } fn update(f: *z.Frame, s: *State) void { z.clearViewport(f, .{ .r = 30, .g = 30, .b = 40, .a = 255 }); // The UI is built first, so its answer to "is the mouse over me?" is known before the scene uses the mouse; it // is drawn last (`render`, below), on top of everything. const u: z.ui_real.Ui = s.ui_host.begin(f); if (u.window("Circle", .{})) |w| { defer w.close(); _ = u.slider("radius", &s.circle_radius, .{ .min = 4, .max = 120, .fmt = "{d:.0} px" }); } const is_mouse_on_ui: bool = u.wantCaptureMouse(); // Responsive coord space - these update on resize / rotation // and the runtime's per-frame ortho reset keeps draw coords // 1:1 with CSS pixels. See zimr.zig per-frame size block. const sw: f32 = f.window.widthf(); const sh: f32 = f.window.heightf(); const cx: f32 = sw / 2; const cy: f32 = sh / 2; const white: Color = .{ .r = 240, .g = 240, .b = 240, .a = 255 }; const dim: Color = .{ .r = 140, .g = 140, .b = 150, .a = 255 }; const accent: Color = .{ .r = 96, .g = 165, .b = 250, .a = 255 }; // Concentric rectangles centred in the canvas. Smallest // dimension caps their size so they stay square-ish on any // aspect ratio (phone portrait, phone landscape, desktop wide). const min_dim: f32 = @min(sw, sh); var i: i32 = 1; while (i <= 4) : (i += 1) { const half: f32 = min_dim * float(i) / 12.0; const rec: z.Rectangle = .{ .x = cx - half, .y = cy - half, .width = 2 * half, .height = 2 * half, }; f.gl.rect( .{ .x = rec.x, .y = rec.y, .width = rec.width, .height = rec.height }, .{ .color = accent, .outline = 2 }, ); } f.gl.text(.{ cx - 90, cy - 18 }, "Hello, World!", .{ .size = 32, .color = white, .font = &s.font }); f.gl.textf( .{ cx - 110, cy + 30 }, "viewport: {d} x {d} CSS px", .{ sw, sh }, .{ .size = 14, .color = dim, .font = &s.font }, ); f.gl.text( .{ 16, sh - 24 }, "move the mouse; drag the slider to resize the circle", .{ .size = 12, .color = dim, .font = &s.font }, ); // The circle at the mouse - but not while the mouse is on the UI window, where it would cover the slider. if (!is_mouse_on_ui) { const mouse: Vec2 = z.getMousePosition(f.input); const circle_color: Color = .{ .r = 250, .g = 180, .b = 60, .a = 200 }; f.gl.circle(mouse, s.circle_radius, .{ .color = circle_color }); f.gl.circle(mouse, s.circle_radius, .{ .color = white, .outline = 2 }); } s.ui_host.render(f); } /// Descriptor-only: the runner (standalone) or a launcher drives this. pub const app: z.AppSpec(State) = .{ .config = .{ .window = .{ .title = "zimr - hello_world", .width = 640, .height = 400, // Logical coordinate space tracks the canvas's CSS // pixels - runtime resets `rlOrtho` each frame so // draw coords are 1:1 with `f.window.screen_width`. .scale_mode = .responsive, }, }, .init = initState, .memory = .managed, .deinit = deinit, .update = update, };
